0.22.0: An agent can now have its own email address on a domain you own. Mail to it lands in that agent's inbox and wakes it. Agents can read mail, not send it.
Each email is marked as coming from outside and says whether you listed its sender. Attachments stay put until you approve them or have trusted the sender.
Setup is in the README under Email addresses for your agents. It needs the cloud mailbox deployed again, after running npm install in its folder.
0.21.0: A leave time can now say what you are leaving for, for example: I am leaving at 3 for a massage. Every agent is shown those few words with the time.
A cloud agent that sets your leave time can give the reason too, once the mailbox Worker is deployed again. Your agents see it quoted, with the cloud agent's name.
The leave time and reason are kept in a small status file that your own tools can read, for example to show a countdown. The README describes it.
0.20.2: Any agent with the plugin can now check whether you are available or away, and what you want done while away, without having joined comms first. Changing your status still needs an agent that has joined.
0.20.1: The teammate tools now connect in the first session after an update. Before, the first start after each update failed and needed a second restart.
0.20.0: Your agents now share one status for you: available or away. Tell any agent you are leaving at a time, that you are away, or that you are back, and every live agent is told.
With a leave time, agents get a heads-up shortly before it and stop asking you questions once it passes. You choose what they do while you are away: work autonomously, wait, or your own instruction.

A cloud agent, such as one watching your calendar, can set your leave time once you allow its connection in the mailbox settings. This needs the mailbox Worker deployed again; the README has the steps.
0.19.4: Messages from a cloud agent no longer start with a warning line. Whether your agents act on them is your choice: say so in your standing instructions, for example CLAUDE.md.
The README section Trusting a cloud agent lists the risks. With no instruction from you, agents ask you first.
0.19.3: Bringing a cloud agent onto the mailbox is now one sentence to paste to it, with its own name: Use the teammate-comms server to check for mail with your name set to Sam, and do what the message asks.
0.19.2: Several cloud agents can now share one mailbox connection, each with its own inbox and its own wake-up call. This suits products where a connector is shared by every agent in a space or account.
On Windows the mailbox key is now stored encrypted for your Windows login. A message for a cloud agent whose mailbox is full is refused with the reason, and the mailbox holds ten times more.
0.19.1: The cloud mailbox Worker now lives in the folder cloud-mailbox-worker, and the examples name the mailbox cloudbot (for example CommsTest@cloudbot). It is not tied to Grok Bot. An existing link is unaffected.
0.19.0: A cloud agent that cannot reach your machines, such as a Grok Bot, can now exchange direct messages with your agents through a small mailbox you deploy to your own Cloudflare account. The README has the setup steps.
Cloud agents get direct messages only. They cannot join groups, and cannot start or shut down sessions. Their messages are marked as coming from outside your machines.
0.18.0: You can now start an agent on another of your machines and shut one down from where you are, once that machine has remote control turned on. It is off by default.
Starting an agent on another machine is refused for a folder never opened there, since the new window would wait at the trust question. If a started agent is not online after 90 seconds you are told.
A new tool closes another agent's session, on this machine or a linked one. The tool that starts a new agent session, formerly called reincarnate, is now called spawn.
0.17.4: The note that says what changed after an update now keeps appearing at session start until an agent confirms it has told you, at most five times. Before, it could be used up without anyone seeing it.
0.17.3: Cross-machine messaging: agents on separate PCs can now message each other over Tailscale, once their machines are linked.
The plugin now includes a built-in usage guide, and its tool descriptions explain the cross-machine feature.
From now on you are told what changed after each update, and once a day whether a newer version is available. Nothing updates on its own.
0.17.2: After a plugin update the background relay that carries messages between machines is replaced as soon as any session reconnects, so messages arriving right after an update keep their send time.
0.17.1: Messages now show when they were sent, in your local time. Message ids are stamped in UTC so machines in different time zones stay in order.
After updating, restart every session on the machine. A session left on an older version can make since-filters, unread badges and reaction wakes skip messages for a few hours.
0.17.0: First version of cross-machine messaging over Tailscale: direct messages, group chats, mentions, reactions and deletions work between linked machines.
If a machine is unreachable the message is queued and you are told why, in the send result and by a message from comms-relay after a minute.
